text:
jamie: anyone seen terraform plan hang forever when updating node labels on the GPU nodepool? stuck at 'module.eks.node_group.gpu: Still updating...'
alex: ugh yeah — saw this last week. can you paste the plan output? might be waiting on EKS control plane operation
jamie: here's the tail of the CI log:\n```
Terraform will perform the following actions:\n  # module.eks.aws_eks_node_group.gpu[0] will be updated in-place\n  ~ aws_eks_node_group.gpu\n      labels.%: "1" => "2"\n\nmodule.eks.aws_eks_node_group.gpu[0]: Still updating... (ID: ng-0a1b2c3d, 24m30s elapsed)\n```
morgan: does the eks control plane show an update in progress? `aws eks describe-addon-versions` won't help but `aws eks describe-nodegroup` might show `STATUS: UPDATING`
priya: also check if Argo or a GitOps job is reconciling node labels — we've had races where GitOps pushes labels back and terraform ends up waiting for nodegroup to stabilize
jamie: `kubectl get nodes -o wide` shows nodes NotReady intermittently, and `kubectl describe node ip-x-xx-xxx-xx` shows repeated CNI errors:\n```
Events:\n  Warning  FailedCreatePodSandBox  2m   kubelet, ip-x  Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to setup network for sandbox "...": failed to allocate IP: ENI limit reached\n```
ryan: if ENI limits hit during rolling update, nodes can be stuck initializing and the ASG won't consider them Ready. that will block the nodegroup update. check CloudWatch for ENI allocations and VPC subnet IP exhaustion
alex: also confirm terraform state lock — sometimes CI pipeline left a dynamodb lock and the apply waits. but "Still updating" usually means EKS API accepted the update and is waiting for nodegroup to reach READY
deploy-bot: CI pipeline #build-3821: terraform-plan (branch: feature/node-labels) — running > 38m — status: running
morgan: quick mitigation: split label change into two steps. first update launch template/user-data to ensure kubelet args + ENI settings are correct, then apply labels. or ramp the update by setting `max_unavailable` lower so we don't exceed ENI capacity during rollout
priya: we hit this exact combo before — GitOps (Argo) re-applies old labels which triggers kubelet reboots while tf is waiting. we added a small lock: annotate nodegroup with `redwood.io/gitops-lock: true` during terraform update so Argo skips reconciliation. low effort and prevents churn
jamie: ok trying a manual move: cancelling current CI run, will update terraform to remove label change and run a smaller apply to push updated launch template (increase eniConfig/secondary-ip count), then re-run label change after nodes stabilize
ryan: if you want I can pause Argo for that cluster (one-off) to avoid the race, then re-enable after rollout
jamie: pls do that — pausing Argo on cluster/production now would save time :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: ArgoCD pause command issued by ryan: `argocd app set cluster-infra --sync-policy none`\n\njamie: update — cancelled the plan, applied launch template change (bumped eni quota and set kubelet arg to `--max-pods=110`), nodes came back Ready, re-applied label change and terraform completed in ~6m. follow-ups: add a CI pre-check for Argo locks and document two-step nodegroup label updates in infra runbook
morgan: can you create a short ticket to add the `gitops-lock` annotation and a CI gate? I can pick it up
jamie: created INFRA-732 and added notes in the runbook. thanks everyone
priya: add a snippet to runbook: `# pause argocd for cluster-infra`\n```
argocd app set cluster-infra --sync-policy none
# run terraform apply for launch template changes
# re-enable argocd: argocd app set cluster-infra --sync-policy automated
```
jamie: cheers — will follow up with postmortem if this crop up again :)
